briefdescription.para: Computes the number of decimal places of a value, with a precision of about seven digits.

detaileddescription.para:
T
The integral type for the result.
Value_T
The type of the input value, a floating-point type.
value
The value whose decimal precision is to be determined; it may be negative, infinite, or a NaN.
The number of decimal places, as a value of type T, at least one, or zero for a zero value; the leading zeros of a value below one are counted; it is limited by the magnitude from which Value_T represents only integers.
This function template determines the number of decimal (fractional) digits present in a floating-point value, with a precision of about seven digits. Being constexpr, it can also be evaluated at compile time.

The function repeatedly multiplies the absolute value by ten, incrementing a counter until the distance to the nearest integer is at most a defined precision threshold (1e-7). Using the distance to the nearest integer, not the fractional part, prevents the rounding noise of a value just below an integer (e.g. 2674.9999999999995) from being taken as more decimals.

The nearest integer is never zero: while the scaled value is below one, its distance to one is used, so that the leading zeros of a small value are counted as decimals, as in its notation (12 for 1e-12), instead of the count stopping as soon as the scaled value is below the threshold. A zero value has no significant digit, and the result is zero.

The loop also stops when the value reaches the magnitude from which the type can represent only integers (2^23 for float, 2^52 for double), limited to 2^63 so that the conversion to unsigned long long is always defined. This bounds the number of steps for large values, infinities, and NaNs, for which the result is one; for small values, the number of steps is bounded by the decimal exponent of the smallest value of the type.

briefdescription.para: Counts the decimal digits of a floating-point literal, before or after the decimal point.

detaileddescription.para: The digit separators (') are not counted.

Fraction
true to count the digits after the decimal point, false to count those before it.
Cs
The characters of the literal.
Parameters
None.
The number of digits.
Walks the characters once, counting the decimal digits before the first decimal point (Fraction false) or after it (Fraction true); the digit separators are skipped.

briefdescription.para: Computes the default comparison tolerance of a floating-point value, one unit of its last decimal.

detaileddescription.para:
Value_T
The type of the value, a floating-point type.
value
The value whose tolerance is to be determined; it may be negative, infinite, or a NaN.
Ten raised to minus the number of decimal places returned by count_decimals() (0.01 for 1.25, 1e-12 for 1e-12), or zero, which means an exact comparison, for a zero value and for a value whose tolerance would be below the range of Value_T.
The number of decimal places is computed by count_decimals(), and the tolerance is one divided by ten raised to that number, as for the floating-point literals, which use the decimals written.

A zero value has no decimals, and gets a zero tolerance, so that it is compared exactly; a tolerance of one unit of an arbitrary decimal would make the zero equal to unrelated small values. A zero tolerance is also returned when ten raised to the number of decimals would exceed the range of Value_T (values below about 1e-308 for double), instead of computing an infinite power.

briefdescription.para: Computes the decimal part of a number represented as an array of characters.

detaileddescription.para:
T
The target integral type for the result.
Cs
The character pack representing the numeric value; it must contain a decimal point.
Parameters
None.
The digits after the decimal point, as an integral value of type T (e.g. 25 for 1.25), to be divided by ten raised to the power returned by den_size().
This function template performs compile-time extraction of the decimal (fractional) part from a sequence of characters, typically provided as a template parameter pack.

The function expects the character sequence to represent a numeric value, where all characters are either digits, a dot (.), or an apostrophe ('). Parsing begins after the first dot, accumulating the decimal digits as an integer value and skipping the digit separators (e.g. 1.25 yields 25), so that den() / 10^den_size() gives the fraction. If the result could exceed T, the compilation fails with an explicit message.

briefdescription.para: Counts the decimal places of a number represented as an array of characters.

detaileddescription.para:
T
The integral type for the result.
Cs
The character pack representing the numeric value; it must contain a decimal point.
Parameters
None.
The number of decimal places (e.g. 2 for 1.25), as a value of type T; it is the scale of the value returned by den().
This function template determines, at compile time, the number of decimal (fractional) digits present in a numeric value represented by a character sequence, typically provided as a template parameter pack.

The function expects the character sequence to represent a numeric value, where all characters are either digits, a dot (.), or an apostrophe ('). It returns the number of digits that follow the first dot (the digit separators are not counted; e.g. 2 for 1.25), which is the scale of the value returned by den().

briefdescription.para: Computes the value of an integer literal of type T, before any negation.

detaileddescription.para:
T
The integral type of the literal.
Cs
The characters of the literal, as received by a literal operator template.
Parameters
None.
The value of the literal, up to max() of T, or, for the signed types, up to max () + 1, the absolute value of the minimum.
The literal must be an integer literal, in any of the C++ forms (decimal, hexadecimal, binary, or octal, with digit separators), and its value must fit in T; otherwise the compilation fails with an explicit message.

Negative values are obtained with the unary minus, so the literal itself is never negative. For the signed types, the limit is the absolute value of the minimum, max () + 1, so that the minimum can be written (e.g. -128_i8); the caller allows this magnitude only when it is negated.
When a check fails, zero is returned, so that the callers report no further errors.

briefdescription.para: Creates the compile-time constant of an integer literal.

detaileddescription.para:
T
The integral type of the literal.
Cs
The characters of the literal, as received by a literal operator template.
Used by the integer literal operators (_i, _u8, etc.).

Parameters
None.
An integral_constant with the value of the literal, or, when the value is the absolute value of the minimum of a signed T, an integral_min_magnitude<T>, valid only when negated.
The value is checked by math::integer_magnitude(), which accepts, for the signed types, the absolute value of the minimum; this value does not fit in T, so it is represented by integral_min_magnitude<T>.

briefdescription.para: Computes the integral part of a decimal floating-point number represented as an array of characters.

detaileddescription.para: Used by the floating-point literal operators; the integer literals use integer_magnitude(), which also accepts the C++ prefixes and checks the range.

T
The target integral type for the result.
Cs
The character pack representing the numeric value.
Parameters
None.
The parsed integral value of type T.
This function template performs compile-time parsing of a numeric value from a sequence of characters, typically provided as a template parameter pack.

The characters must be decimal digits, a dot (.), or digit separators ('), which are skipped; otherwise (e.g. an exponent) the compilation fails with an explicit message, as it does if the integral part has more digits than T can always hold. Parsing stops at the first dot, allowing the function to extract only the integral part of the number.

briefdescription.para: Parses the characters of an integer literal.

detaileddescription.para:
Cs
The characters of the literal, as received by a literal operator template.
Parameters
None.
The value, and whether the characters form an integer literal and whether its value fits in unsigned long long.
The characters are those of a valid C++ literal, already checked by the compiler (digits valid for the base, digit separators in valid positions). The base is given by the prefix: 0x or 0X for hexadecimal, 0b or 0B for binary, a leading 0 for octal, and none for decimal. The digit separators (') are skipped.

Any other character (a decimal point, an exponent, or a digit not valid for the base, as in the floating-point literal 09.5) marks the literal as not an integer. The value is accumulated in unsigned long long, and the accumulation stops if it would overflow.

memberdef.argsstring: (const T base, const Exp_T exp) noexcept
memberdef.name: pow

briefdescription.para: Generic exponentiation function to compute the power of a base raised to an exponent.

detaileddescription.para:
T
The type of the base value. Must support multiplication assignment and construction from an integer.
Exp_T
The type of the exponent. Must be default-constructible (to zero), and support the < and prefix ++ operators.
base
The base value to be raised to the power of exp.
exp
The exponent value.
The result of raising base to the power of exp.
This function template provides a constexpr implementation for raising a base value to a given exponent, supporting any types that allow multiplication.
The function starts from one and multiplies the result by the base exp times. If the exponent is zero (or negative), the function returns one (the multiplicative identity for the type).

briefdescription.para: C++ header file with inline implementations for the deprecated µTest++ definitions.

detaileddescription.para: This header provides the inline implementations for the deprecated definitions declared in deprecated.h: the v5.0.1 names of the logical functions (_not, _and, and _or), which forward to negate(), all_of(), and any_of(), mut(), the overloaded operators, the user-defined literals, and approx (value, epsilon), and the members of the detail::timestamp class.
The constructor of detail::timestamp that reads the system clock is defined in src/deprecated.cpp, with detail::read_clock(), the clock access used by detail::stopwatch.
All definitions reside within the micro_os_plus::micro_test_plus namespace.
This file is included by deprecated.h; the applications include micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus.h, not this file.
